ops.new_text: The last four are numerical approximation components. The first is separately typed input or model-enclosure uncertainty. A defensible enclosure would require a declared roof norm, an operator norm, and an output norm; a stability statement from roof perturbation to operator perturbation; a legal coefficient map between orbit and projected-operator representations; propagation of all five bounds through the chosen approximation chain; and a determinant-conditioning estimate on the declared complex domain. Without these links, even individually small terms cannot be called additive, exhaustive, or complete. Within the retained project evidence, no dedicated project roundoff theorem, geometry-input theorem, common norm, or determinant-conditioning bound has been established.

The theorem template distinguishes local calibration from a uniform enclosure. Its required fields are \path{input_space}, \path{roof_norm}, \path{operator_space}, \path{complex_domain}, \path{operator_map}, \path{coefficient_map}, \path{raw_channels}, \path{dependency_ledger}, \path{conditioning_functional}, \path{output_functional}, and \path{output_tolerance}. Agreement at selected parameters or on a precision ladder may test code paths but cannot fill any theorem field. Conditioning near zeros or spectral features must be included in \(\kappa_D\). The Gate-5 comparison window \(\Omega\) is fixed, but no instantiated error theorem certifies validity on that window. The constants, output-functional tolerance, and all raw bounds remain \texttt{UNASSIGNED}, and \path{complex_domain} is not yet bound to a justified theorem-validity domain; hence the template is type-readable but \path{ERROR_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUABLE}.

The second finding is that the \texttt{d=6a} physical-roof certificate requires a complete object map from collision geometry through roof regularity and normalization to an eligible operator space and determinant convention. The synthesis identifies candidate components, but the instantiated map has not been established in the retained project evidence. Fitting a pointwise roof from inherited periodic totals remains prohibited.

A future scientific package would require deterministic schemas for geometry, roof, operator, coefficients, errors, and controls. They would record \texttt{a}, \texttt{d=6a}, the section and collision inputs; pointwise evaluator bytes and roof uncertainty; operator space, domain, potential, basis, and determinant convention; orbit-to-trace coefficient bindings; all five error channels with norm, stability, propagation, dependency, and conditioning witnesses; and typed physical, unit, cyclic-label symmetry, and neighboring-geometry roofs.

No pointwise roof, exact section, operator, function space, coefficient map, rank, quadrature, precision ladder, determinant, error bound, physical period validation, control roof, or nontransfer witness is constructed or evaluated. Within the retained project evidence, no project-specific roundoff theorem, geometry-input theorem, common norm, roof-to-operator stability estimate, propagation theorem, or determinant-conditioning bound has been established. The five-channel contract is therefore a prospective architecture, not a complete total error.

Any later execution package should expose the smallest evidence unit that permits independent failure diagnosis. The geometry layer should carry disk and section conventions, collision points, interval inputs, and pointwise flight evaluations. The operator layer should carry the potential, normalization, space, complex domain, and field-by-field hypothesis map. The coefficient layer should record primitive words, repetitions, trace conventions, projection indices, and the exact comparison theorem being used. The error layer should preserve every raw bound before composition, including its norm, constants, dependencies, and valid domain. The control layer should serialize physical, unit, cyclic-label symmetry, and neighboring-geometry roofs through the same callable interface.

The retained project evidence motivates a program for testing whether a classical determinant belongs to the physical \texttt{d=6a} three-disk flow; it does not establish such a determinant. The present article preserves the type firewall, turns roof-agnostic calibration into an explicit design principle, and replaces an under-specified four-part total-error claim with a five-channel proof obligation: four numerical components plus separately propagated geometry/roof-input uncertainty under one norm, stability, propagation, and conditioning contract.

Accordingly, the minimum physical-determinant certificate consists of Gates~1--5 in \path{PASSED} state under one hash-linked dependency chain. Gate~6 is a separately activated directional module: \path{NOT_ACTIVATED} is reported when its pre-result roof-pair, relation, theorem map, and predicate record is absent; an activated module terminates only as \path{NONTRANSFER_CERTIFIED} or \path{NONTRANSFER_NOT_PROVED}. At present Gates~1--5 are \path{NOT_STARTED} and Gate~6 is \path{NOT_ACTIVATED}; the manuscript supplies only the prospective decision structure and reports no physical, analytic, numerical, control, cohomological, or Route result.
